subject: StellarMetrics - volume thresholds and legal conditions for hosted API pricing
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice.c@stellarmetrics.com>, procurement@stellarmetrics.com
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: StellarMetrics — hosted API volume tiers & legal gating questions

Hi Alice (and procurement team),

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — great discussion on your high-throughput ingestion use case. I promised a concise summary of the pricing structure we discussed and a couple of options that map to the volume profile you shared (200M–1B tokens / month). Attached is a quick worksheet with example tiers.

Two quick clarifying asks from your side before we draft a formal quote: 1) does your legal/procurement team require a signed DPA and SOC2 evidence before a committed spend is accepted? and 2) are you able to sign a standard Redwood DPA, or will you need redlines?

What I can offer today:
- Per-token hosted pricing with three commit tiers (200M, 500M, 1B) and stepped discounts as shown in the attached Pricing_Worksheet.xlsx.
- If you need DPA/SOC2 in place first, we can provisionally hold the quoted pricing for 30 days while legal completes review (we ask for an LOI or purchase order to reserve capacity).

If legal requires DPA redlines we’ll loop in SalesOps and Legal — typically our legal team can accept minimal redlines related to data retention and security, but we need to see the requested changes.

Next steps: can you confirm who on your side will own the DPA review? If you prefer, I can send our standard DPA and our latest SOC2 report now.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[rachel.kim@redwood.com]

Attachments: Pricing_Worksheet.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Alice Chen <alice.c@stellarmetrics.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@stellarmetrics.com, Ivan Legal <ivan.legal@stellarmetrics.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: StellarMetrics — hosted API volume tiers & legal gating questions

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the clear recap and the worksheet. We reviewed internally — the pricing tiers look promising. A couple of constraints from procurement/legal:

- Our procurement policy requires a signed DPA and evidence of SOC2 Type II (or equivalent) prior to executing any multi-month committed spend. We can make an exception for small POCs but not for an initial committed contract at the volumes we discussed.
- Our legal team will provide a list of requested redlines; we typically push on data residency, vendor subcontractors, and breach notification SLAs.

I’ve CC’d Ivan (legal) and procurement. Ivan, can you confirm an expected turnaround if Redwood provides the SOC2 report and the latest DPA?

If Redwood can share the SOC2 attestation and a clean DPA copy today, procurement can start the internal PR and approval flow. We prefer to avoid heavy redlines but will ask for specific tweaks if needed.

Appreciate the 30-day hold offer — that helps.

Best,
Alice Chen
Head of Data Platforms | StellarMetrics
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Chen <alice.c@stellarmetrics.com>, Ivan Legal <ivan.legal@stellarmetrics.com>, procurement@stellarmetrics.com
Date: Sat, 27 Jun 2026 08:32:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: StellarMetrics — hosted API volume tiers & legal gating questions

Team — forwarding StellarMetrics' response. Quick summary and asks:

Summary: they require executed DPA + SOC2 evidence before signing a committed tier. They will try to avoid heavy redlines but Ivan/legal will send desired changes.

Asks:  
- Marissa: can we approve a 30-day pricing hold for the quoted tiers while DPA gets reviewed? If yes, I’ll include that language in the email to Alice.
- Neha: can you confirm we can share the SOC2 Type II attestation and if any additional material (security architecture summary) is advisable to attach?
- Marcus: any constraints from product/security on accepting DPA redlines around data residency or retention? Also, confirm whether we can add a conditional-sign clause: pricing is honored for 30 days pending DPA execution, after which we reserve the right to reprice.

I’ve attached the Pricing_Worksheet in the original thread. Happy to jump on a quick 20-min sync if helpful.

Thanks,
Rachel

-----Forwarded message attached above-----
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Chen <alice.c@stellarmetrics.com>, Ivan Legal <ivan.legal@stellarmetrics.com>, procurement@stellarmetrics.com
Date: Wed, 1 Jul 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: StellarMetrics — hosted API volume tiers & legal gating questions

Thanks for looping me in, Rachel. Recommend the following approach:

1) Immediate: share our SOC2 Type II attestation and standard DPA (see attached SOC2_Report-Redwood-2025.pdf and our DPA draft). That should unblock procurement's initial review. Neha — please attach the SOC2 and a short one-page security summary.

2) Pricing hold: approve a 30-calendar-day pricing hold tied to receipt of an LOI or an intent-to-sign note from StellarMetrics. Language suggestion to use in the email: "Redwood will honor the quoted per-token tier pricing for 30 days from receipt of buyer’s written intent to proceed, provided Redwood receives a draft of the buyer’s redlines (if any) and makes good faith efforts to negotiate the DPA to mutual execution. If the DPA is not executed within 30 days, Redwood reserves the right to adjust pricing based on capacity and rate changes."

3) Redlines: we should accept limited, commercially reasonable redlines on data retention, liability cap (within our standard ranges), and confidentiality carve-outs. Anything that requires changes to our core platform operations (data residency or changes to caching behavior) should be escalated to Marcus for product/security assessment.

4) Optional commercial sweetener: offer a $25k onboarding credit (applied toward first-month usage) if they sign within 30 days — this often speeds procurement. If StellarMetrics pushes back on the credit, keep it as our fallback.

I’m attaching the SOC2 attestation and a clean DPA for them to review.

Marissa Cole
Director, Sales — Enterprise Accounts | Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOC2_Report-Redwood-2025.pdf (PDF), Redwood_Standard_DPA_v2.docx (document)
From: Ivan Legal <ivan.legal@stellarmetrics.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Chen <alice.c@stellarmetrics.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, procurement@stellarmetrics.com
Date: Sat, 4 Jul 2026 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: StellarMetrics — hosted API volume tiers & legal gating questions

Rachel / Marissa — thanks for the quick follow-up and for sharing the SOC2 report and the DPA copy. We’ve completed an initial review and can proceed under the following conditions: 

1) We confirm receipt of the SOC2 Type II attestation (received).
2) We have a DPA with two minor redlines: a) clarify data deletion timing after contract termination (we propose 45 days), and b) add a subcontractor disclosure clause that requires notice within 30 days of onboarding any third-party processor.

Those are reasonable asks and not showstoppers. Procurement expects a clean counter with those adjustments; after we get the updated DPA we will aim to route for signature within 10 business days. We will also issue an LOI indicating intent to proceed (to reserve the pricing hold).

If Redwood can circulate an updated DPA reflecting those two bullets and confirm the 30-day pricing hold and the onboarding credit option, I’ll push this through legal/procurement ASAP.

Thanks,
Ivan Legal
Senior Counsel | StellarMetrics
